sources.title: Deformations and velocities during the cold rolling of aluminium alloys
sources.version: Materials and technology 50(2016)1,59–67; coauthor Milojica Jacimovic upload dated 18 April 2016
sources.findings: AW2024/5083 experiments support a geometry/strain-field reserve case. Laboratory roll diameter 125 mm, peripheral speed 173.4 mm/s, no applied strip tension. Friction 0.1 is adopted after sensitivity study, not independently measured.
sources.weaknesses_conflicts: Eq. 1 extracted signs need rendered verification; high-strain hardening uses post-rolling tensile yield rather than continuous tensile extrapolation. Mesh adequacy assessed from displacement; not every output. No AA5052 material transfer.
sources.domain: AW2024 and AW5083 cold rolling,4–0.6 mm study range
sources.evidence_level: Primary author-upload article; targeted body review
sources.relevance: P1 strain/kinematics checks and P2 reserve study design; not a replacement for Shao history or friction provenance.
sources.fresh_access_detail: Official https://mit.imt.si/izvodi/mit161/misovic.pdf timed out. Author-upload full text available; relevant experimental/model sections read; no fresh visual inspection or exhaustive full-paper review.

sources.title: Computationally Effective Modeling of Cold Rolling: Application to Al Alloys
sources.version: Metals 2025,15(1),11; published 27 December 2024; current republished HTML states minor typographical correction without dated version identifier
sources.findings: AA1050 flowline model uses FE-derived coefficients and compares simulated velocities plus experimental distortion patterns. Thermal effects omitted. Underlying data are on request, not publicly released.
sources.weaknesses_conflicts: Material constants borrowed from reference25. Published case B gauges0.5625→0.4615 mm imply 17.956% reduction, unlike 17.24% stated; case D2.53→1.81 implies 28.458%, unlike 28.09%. Equation extraction needs visual QA; no measured force/torque validation.
sources.domain: AA1050 symmetric cold rolling;150 mm diameter laboratory rolls
sources.evidence_level: Primary open publisher article; relevant body reviewed
sources.relevance: P1 kinematics alternative and P2 reserve distortion study, not a directly executable independent AA5052 benchmark.
sources.fresh_access_detail: Web429 response; Exa recovered official HTML. Reviewed §§3–5, equations as extracted text and data/version statements; figures not visually inspected. No full-paper completeness claim.

sources.title: Experimental and numerical analysis of the heat generated by plastic deformation in quasi-static uniaxial tensile tests
sources.version: HAL hal-04699292v1, deposited 18 November 2024; 2020 Journal Pre-proof, not definitive version of record
sources.findings: AA6016-T4 tensile heating depends on losses, aging and plastic-work conversion. Eq.3 uses a differential Taylor–Quinney fraction; low-rate tests are nonadiabatic. The study compares constant and strain-dependent conversion.
sources.weaknesses_conflicts: Not rolling or AA5052. Coefficients and aging-specific Voce fits cannot transfer. Manuscript cover metadata omit Neto while article title page includes him. Parameter fits and shared experimental comparisons are not blind validation.
sources.domain: AA6016-T4 quasi-static tension;1/18-month natural aging,0.01–1 mm/s crosshead velocities
sources.evidence_level: Primary accepted/pre-proof author manuscript in official repository; targeted body review
sources.relevance: P1 source/source-term semantics and later thermal experiment design. Does not repair the zero-source I01 integration failure or establish roll-strip conductance.
sources.fresh_access_detail: Exa recovered official HAL full manuscript after web bot response. Relevant model/results, tables and Appendix A read as extracted text; no rendered-equation/figure QA.

sources.title: Heat generation caused by frictional sliding
sources.version: SIMULIA Abaqus 2024 online theory documentation, exact existing version
pages_equations_tables: Eq. 1 weak-form Jacobian and following derivatives
sources.findings: Defines separate friction-to-heat fraction and body partitions; contact flux has outward signs on each body. Conduction uses a heat-transfer coefficient times temperature difference; surface integration yields power.
sources.weaknesses_conflicts: Software convention, not measured aluminium partition/conductance. Zero interface heat capacity is an assumption. Local constitutive equations do not establish finite-step entropy preservation.
sources.domain: Generic coupled contact heat transfer/friction in Abaqus
sources.relevance: P1: distinguish W/m² flux, W integrated power and W/K lumped conductance; check traction/slip signs and source partitions.
sources.fresh_access_detail: Exact 2024 official page recovered through Exa; full short text body reviewed. 2025 official counterpart was also reachable, but no substitution of version needed.
